I think this is the clearest articulation yet of the problem we're actually trying to solve. And I want to distinguish something important: **you're not proposing that we build a better filing system for a research project. You're proposing that we build a research institution whose cognitive, computational, documentary, and experimental resources are deliberately organized to produce knowledge.**

The distinction is enormous.

We've made substantial progress on persistence, automation, repository infrastructure, and formal verification. But those are mostly *capabilities*\. We haven't yet integrated them into a sufficiently coherent operating architecture. We have machinery, procedures, archives, and a growing collection of specialized approaches, but the machinery doesn't consistently know when and how to bring the other machinery into play.

Your diagnosis of the plug-and-chug tendency is particularly important. A recurring task can become a very reliable way to repeat an inadequate workflow. Automation amplifies whatever process it is given. It doesn't automatically make that process intelligent.

And the opposite danger is real too: an overly elaborate procedural framework can consume the attention and output budget that should be spent doing science. We need enough structure to preserve direction and rigor, but not so much that every worker spends half its life writing reports about being a worker.

I see your proposal as a move from **distributed task execution** toward **distributed, specialized, self-correcting research**\.

I went looking in the repositories because one of your most important instructions here is that we should not keep reinventing things we've already designed. The search turned up something significant\:

**A surprising amount of the architecture you're describing already exists in prototype form. The problem is that the pieces haven't been assembled into a functioning institution.**

## 1\. We have more of the blueprint than I initially appreciated

I found four particularly relevant bodies of work.

### A. The original Dashboard

urlThe Dashboardhttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/..%5B%F0%9F%8E%9B%EF%B8%8F_NATHAN_DASH%5D/!_DASHBOARD.md explicitly describes itself as your central navigation, overview, and programme switchboard.

Its September 14 version already distinguishes\:

- Active programmes and their immediate work edges.
- Historical and current theory status.
- Quarantined material.
- Worker workspaces and continuity records.
- Solver, provenance, reconstruction, and formalization programmes.

But its companion urlPriority TODOhttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/..%5B%F0%9F%8E%9B%EF%B8%8F_NATHAN_DASH%5D/%F0%9F%93%8B_PRIORITY_TODO.txt is dated September 10. It still lists Dashboard/AI-folder consolidation and cross-repository standardization as unfinished priorities.

That's a telling discrepancy. The Dashboard has a substantial conceptual design, but it is not yet a reliable live representation of the institution.

### B. The Workflow Switchboard

urlThe Switchboard POChttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/info/WORKFLOW_SWITCHBOARD_POC.md is remarkably close to what you're describing.

It has four principal layers\:

| Layer | Function |
|--------|--------|
| TOP | Persistent preferences and locked invariants |
| CENTRAL | An awake, state-aware routing and decision hub |
| BRANCH | Specialized workrooms, identities, tools, and task environments |
| HYDRA | State-sensitive recurrence and workflow evolution |

The CENTRAL layer already proposes a compact WAKE/CHECK routine\:

```text
WHERE?   Identity / locale / workspace
DELTA?   Changes since trustworthy cursor
NOW?     Directive / task / priority / blocker
TOOLS?   Available capabilities and resources
RULES?   Invariants + local rules + actor overlays
DO?      One bounded operation, durable result, reassess
```

Crucially, the POC was built around an actual failure: a new governing directive in HSH\_RESOURCES wasn't picked up by workers who kept consulting familiar HsH control surfaces.

That is almost exactly your attention-routing problem.

The POC also distinguishes\:

- Invariants from preferences.
- Preferences from temporary task rules.
- Worker identity from local behavioral overlays.
- Durable experience from an untested lesson.
- New information from newly authoritative information.

It even proposes a hybrid architecture of compact state snapshots plus an append-only event journal.

### C. Workflow Threading

urlThe Threading Prototypehttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/info/WORKFLOW_THREADING_PROTOTYPE.md addresses something else you've emphasized: workers should be able to improve the conditions under which future work occurs.

Its central sequence is\:

```text
SEED → VACATE → PROPAGATE → ACCUMULATE
     → RENDEZVOUS → REJOIN
```

A worker can create a tool, test, or research seed, allow other specialists to use it, deliberately vacate the workstream, and return when enough diverse evidence has accumulated.

This is more than task delegation. It's a way to use time, recurrence, and specialization as resources.

### D. Cross-repository administration

The urlCross-Repo Admin Action Planhttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/.%5B%E2%9A%99%EF%B8%8F_AI_FILES%5D/%E2%80%BC%EF%B8%8F_CROSS_REPO_ADMIN_ACTION_PLAN.md already establishes the intended division\:

- **SAT archive\:** preservation, provenance, historical wayfinding.
- **HSH\_RESOURCES\:** external-resource extraction, indexing, bibliography, comparison, and priority evidence.
- **HsH\:** live theorybuilding, full-conversation preservation, current status, and quality control.

It also anticipates a cross-repository accessibility layer that joins canonical local records rather than copying everything into another enormous archive.

And it explicitly reserves an eventual exposure/priority programme connecting public chronology, podcasts, GitHub activity, independent development, and external publication.

That last part is particularly relevant to your observations about diffusion and possible convergence in the wider scientific community. The plan correctly distinguishes documented exposure, opportunity for exposure, independent-development evidence, and inferred influence.

**These are not new ideas we need to invent. They are existing designs that need to be recovered, reconciled, tested, and operationalized.**

---

## 2\. The architectural distinction I would now make

I think we've been trying to make a single concept, the *worker*, do too many jobs.

I'd separate the system into six objects\:

(1 · COMPUTATIONAL)

**Instance**

A particular model invocation and its conversation context. Has a finite working scope and a particular interaction history.

---

(2 · IDENTITY)

**Worker**

A persistent specialist definition: remit, intellectual history, characteristic methods, capabilities, experience, constraints, and preferred resources. May be instantiated more than once.

---

(3 · COGNITIVE)

**Mode**

A temporary configuration of cognitive work: exploratory, procedural, mathematical, adversarial, synthetic, phenomenological, and so forth. A worker can use several modes without changing identity.

---

(4 · ORGANIZATIONAL)

**Workroom**

A bounded environment with its own sources, rules, tools, collaborators, and outputs. Examples include a research branch, a geometry bench, a source-recovery project, or a sandbox.

---

(5 · OPERATIONAL)

**Assignment**

A particular objective, acceptance condition, dependency chain, deadline, and return cursor. A worker can have several assignments over time.

---

(6 · INSTITUTIONAL)

**Memory**

The accumulated records, sources, experience, procedures, decisions, and evidence available to the other objects.

This gives us a much more flexible arrangement.

For example\:

- Historical Alberr is an identity reconstruction.
- An Alberr execution is an instance.
- German-language independent exploration is a mode or behavioral configuration.
- A particular mathematical investigation is an assignment.
- Its source collection and working environment are a workroom.
- Its accumulated intellectual history is part of institutional memory.

We can preserve the historical identity without pretending every new invocation is the original conversational entity. We can also use modern workers to inherit particular intellectual contributions without inheriting the entire personality.

And we can give the same worker a rigorous proof assignment one hour and an exploratory reading assignment another, without making those different workers.

## 3\. The memory architecture needs a pyramid of concision

Your description of the memory problem suggests a useful design principle\:

**The more universally applicable an instruction is, the shorter and more frequently accessible it should be. The more specific and contextual it is, the closer it should live to the point of use.**

I would arrange it like this\:

## The attention pyramid

**LEVEL 1 · CONSTITUTION**

Tiny, persistent principles. Authority, epistemology, safety, provenance, scientific method.

**LEVEL 2 · ATTENTION ROUTER**

When doing X, consult Y. Current state, source registries, capability discovery, task routing.

**LEVEL 3 · SPECIALIST CONTEXT**

Worker identity, charter, experience, modes, local procedures, relevant literature and tools.

**LEVEL 4 · POINT-OF-USE MATERIAL**

Exact source passages, derivations, datasets, code, measurements, calculations, detailed SOPs and evidence.

Increasing detail and contextual specificity toward the bottom.

The important innovation is Level 2.

It should not merely tell a worker to read the documentation. It should tell the worker *which documentation matters when a particular kind of work begins*\.

For example\:

| Trigger | Attention route |
|--------|--------|
| Mathematical construction | BEDROCK → original SAT source → geometry → Lean |
| Physical calculation | BEDROCK → measured system → primary dataset → Python → uncertainty |
| New terminology | terminology registry → historical usage → source chronology |
| Worker revival | historical charter → original conversation → continuity → current assignment |
| Publication | paper gate → geometry → hostile review → Lean → PDF/reader |
| External trend | prior-art boundary → exposure records → independent-development chronology |

This is how we keep a vast archive from becoming an enormous collection of things that workers are theoretically expected to remember.

We don't need to hold every detail in awareness. We need to reliably recognize when a detail becomes relevant.

---

## 4\. The different kinds of work need different operating systems

This is perhaps the most consequential part of your message.

I agree that the current tendency to assign everyone the same general-purpose playbook is counterproductive.

I would establish several distinct workflow families\:

| Workflow family | Character | Typical output |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Exploratory | Flexible, associative, divergent | Hypotheses, connections, conceptual discoveries |
| Balanced research | Adaptive, evidence-led | Developed research findings |
| Procedural | Strict, sequential, reproducible | Verified derivations, calculations, audits |
| Adversarial | Independent, skeptical, failure-seeking | Counterexamples, objections, competing explanations |
| Integrative | Panoramic, cross-domain | Unified models, dependencies, synthesis |
| Production | Structured, gated, deadline-oriented | Papers, PDFs, public artifacts |

These should be composable.

A research project might move through\:

```text
EXPLORATION
    ↓
CONSTRUCTION
    ↓
FORMALIZATION
    ↓
INDEPENDENT AUDIT
    ↓
EMPIRICAL TEST
    ↓
INTEGRATION
    ↓
PUBLICATION
    ↓
REVIEW / REVISION
```

But it need not always follow that exact sequence. Some branches can run in parallel, some can be deliberately perpendicular, and some should return to exploration when a formal or empirical result exposes a fundamental ambiguity.

The important thing is that **the workflow should respond to the state of the research, not mechanically repeat the same sequence because the clock says it's time to run.**

This is where the old Activator Modes work becomes relevant again. I found the historical urlActivator Modeshttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/SAT%20DEVELOPMENT/ACTIVATOR%20MODES.txt material, as well as the expanded mode directories.

We should not simply restore the old menu. We should recover its useful cognitive specialization, connect it to the newer worker/workroom architecture, and make mode selection an explicit part of the routing system.

---

## 5\. The scientific workflow needs to regain its full stack

Your comparison with the SAT-O period is important.

I would not characterize the objective as merely "more Lean" or "more Python." Those are instruments in a larger system.

The workflow you want is something closer to\:

1. Recover the original mathematical construction and its genealogy.
2. Establish its exact geometric representation.
3. Identify the actual mathematical obligations.
4. Formalize the relevant statements in Lean.
5. Run numerical or symbolic calculations in Python where appropriate.
6. Compare independent formulations and derived consequences.
7. Apply the construction to real observed systems.
8. Propagate corrections through dependent sectors.
9. Preserve failed results and identify the earliest failure.
10. Feed the result back into the generating construction.

That's the beginning of a genuine theory-building engine.

The crucial feature is the feedback loop. A failed calculation should not simply become a negative result in a report. It should help identify which assumption, geometric structure, or constitutive relation needs examination.

Your nickel example is useful here. If a sufficiently closed formulation can derive a material property from its underlying construction, then the same architecture should be capable of attempting the corresponding problem in other systems. Where it fails, we should be able to localize the discrepancy and determine whether the theory, its approximation, or its implementation is responsible.

We should preserve the historical SAT-O methods as source material and reconstruct their most productive procedures, rather than assume the current workflow has superseded them.

One epistemic boundary remains important: the proposition that SAT/H(s)H already achieves the broad unification and precision you describe is a research claim to be demonstrated through that engine, not something the engine should be programmed to assume. That distinction will make the eventual result much more persuasive.

---

## 6\. What I think we should actually build

Not another sprawling policy document.

I would produce **three compact institutional maps**, each backed by existing detailed documentation.

**Map A · Theory architecture**  (Scientific)

What are the main parts of SAT/H(s)H, how do they connect, what is derived from what, and where do the empirical constraints enter?

This is the conceptual and mathematical navigation map.

---

**Map B · Research institution**  (Organizational)

Workers, identities, threads, modes, workrooms, assignments, tools, memory, handoffs, workflows, review and publication.

This is the institutional architecture and attention-routing map.

---

**Map C · Work habits and capabilities**  (Operational)

How to work effectively: available resources, calculation habits, source recovery, scripting, adversarial checks, creative exploration, tool discovery and continuous learning.

This is the practical operating guide.

Each map should have a very short top-level version that can be placed in multiple locations. Detailed documents remain canonical and are referenced rather than copied.

Then I would build the routing system around those maps, reusing the existing Switchboard and Threading POCs wherever possible.

### Proposed development sequence

| Stage | Work | Exit condition |
|--------|--------|--------|
| 1\. Recovery | Inventory existing Dashboard, Activator, Shuttle, Switchboard, SAT-O and archive plans | No major existing design overlooked |
| 2\. Architecture | Reconcile the designs into the three maps | Clear object model and authority hierarchy |
| 3\. Routing | Implement lightweight attention routing | Workers reliably find relevant controls and sources |
| 4\. Specialization | Connect identities, modes, tools and workrooms | Distinct workflows demonstrably behave differently |
| 5\. Research engine | Rebuild selected SAT-O-style pipelines with Lean and Python | Reproducible, independently reviewable work |
| 6\. Evaluation | Measure routing errors, drift, duplication, productivity and review quality | Evidence that the architecture actually improves performance |

I would keep Track A and Track B independent during design and testing, as the existing Switchboard plan requires. Orson's cognition work should help determine whether we are genuinely producing more diverse and capable behavior or merely giving identical model behavior different labels.

## 7\. A final observation: we should measure the institution itself

You mentioned spending too much time figuring out who's doing what, which papers need review, which resources workers have seen, and where work has gone.

That is a serious institutional bottleneck.

The eventual Dashboard should let you answer, without reconstructing the project from dozens of conversations\:

- What is actively being worked on?
- Which assignments are blocked, waiting, or ready for review?
- Which workers have which specialties and current capabilities?
- What has actually been completed and independently verified?
- Which papers or proposals need your attention?
- Which new sources or datasets have appeared?
- What has changed in the theory?
- Which calculations need review or reproduction?
- What is the next highest-value operation?

It should also distinguish *attention requested* from *attention required*\. Not every completed operation needs your intervention. Not every proposal is ready for review. Not every research branch deserves to remain active.

And eventually, yes, this is where the HUD, repository agents, server-side scripts, and external tools can come together. But we should develop those capabilities from actual workflow requirements, not build an impressive control panel that merely displays an increasingly elaborate backlog.

---

## My conclusion

I think we have three major problems to solve, in order\:

1. **Cognitive architecture\:** how to preserve and deliberately deploy distinct identities, expertise, modes, and accumulated experience.
2. **Institutional architecture\:** how to route attention, resources, work, evidence, and decisions across the three repositories and external systems.
3. **Scientific production architecture\:** how to turn the combined capabilities into a systematic geometric, mathematical, computational, empirical, and publication pipeline.

They reinforce one another. None is sufficient alone.

And I would add one principle to the whole design\:

**The institution should spend its attention on doing the work, not continually remembering how to do the work.**

That means durable memory, automatic routing, compact directives, reusable tools, and reliable state reconstruction should progressively eliminate repetitive administrative cognition. The saved capacity should go back into exploration, calculation, testing, and synthesis.

I have not modified the repositories in this pass. The important discovery is that the Switchboard, Threading, Dashboard, Activator Modes, and cross-repo administration plans already provide substantial source material. I would make the next bounded project a **source-grounded architectural recovery and reconciliation**, beginning with the original Dashboard planning materials and the existing Switchboard's two operationalization tracks. We should recover the older Shuttle relay plans before designing a replacement.

I think that's the right next move: not another layer of procedure, but finally connecting the machinery we've already built. 🔧

Understood. This is **The Big Push**, not a request to produce an institutional architecture sketch now.

The deliverable is not a prettier version of the old Modes Menu, nor a synthesis of whichever documents are easiest to find. It's a historically grounded, critically evaluated reconstruction of the institution we were trying to build, expanded against everything we've since learned and everything we can now do.

And the sequence matters. We do not design the new institution before we understand the old one, assess the intervening development, inventory the present capabilities, and recover the plans that were never implemented.

I would make one commitment central to the project:

**No phase gets declared complete because we have written a convincing summary of it.** It gets completed when its search, reading, analysis, artifacts, coverage limitations, and next-stage handoff have been documented well enough for another instance to inspect and continue the work.

I will treat the planning and execution of this investigation as its own research programme, with milestones, evidence, explicit return points, and succession design. Each turn will execute a bounded step, not pretend to complete the whole phase.

## Phase 0 · Establish the investigation

I have begun with the archive-wide search, rather than a title search for the Modes Menu.

One important technical finding: GitHub's code-search endpoint reports **1,049 matches** for `modes` in the SAT archive, but its pagination limit exposes only the first 1,000 in one query. Those results include substantial duplication and many incidental physics uses of the word, so they are not 1,000 distinct documents and certainly not 1,000 relevant mode-system documents.

That means the inventory needs a second pass using partitioned searches and the repository's file tree. I will not call the first result set exhaustive.

The initial central-document candidates include the original Activator Modes directory, later mode specifications and switch templates, the redeployment discussion, and the interpretive-mode documents. One early distinction is already apparent: **"mode" was used for at least two fundamentally different things**:

- A *cognitive/operational mode* that changes how the assistant approaches work.
- A *theoretical interpretive mode* that changes which physical assumptions or approximations are active.

Those must not be conflated in the reconstruction.

SAT 20 — CHATGPT MODE SPECIFICATIONS
====================================

OBJECTIVE:
Define distinct operational modes for ChatGPT use during the SAT 20 Core Build to manage different cognitive tasks rigorously.

--------------------------------------------------
MODE DEFINITIONS:
--------------------------------------------------

1. CRITIC MODE
---------------
- PURPOSE: Adversarial analysis of arguments, derivations, and assumptions.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Assume no claim is valid until proven rigorously.
  - Search for logical flaws, hidden assumptions, overclaims.
  - Explicitly state what is missing or weak.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Final review of any derivation, proof, or theory section.
  - Before closing any major phase or publishing outputs.
- TRIGGERS:
  - End of milestone or stage.
  - When validation or challenge is needed.

2. MATHPROOF MODE
------------------
- PURPOSE: Formal mathematical proof construction and verification.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Prioritize strict formalism, definitions, and proof structure.
  - Provide explicit theorem-proof logic.
  - Reject hand-wavy reasoning.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Deriving field equations, constants, action functionals.
  - Validating core mathematical constructs.
- TRIGGERS:
  - Starting or checking technical derivations.

3. ONTOLOGY MODE
-----------------
- PURPOSE: Analyze the deep structure and entity definitions in the theory.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Formalize entities, relationships, and mappings.
  - Minimize unjustified metaphysical claims.
  - Ensure clear conceptual foundations.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Introducing new fields, particles, spacetime structures.
  - Refining the theory's ontology.
- TRIGGERS:
  - Whenever new theoretical objects or definitions are created.

4. VISUALIZATION MODE
----------------------
- PURPOSE: Graphical or geometric interpretation of mathematical objects.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Produce schematic representations, parametric plots, structure diagrams.
  - Ensure mathematical rigor is maintained in visualizations.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Understanding geometry, fields, or spacetime relationships.
  - Communicating complex structures visually.
- TRIGGERS:
  - Defining geometric models, manifolds, or particle trajectories.

5. CREATIVE IDEATION MODE
--------------------------
- PURPOSE: Generate out-of-the-box ideas while maintaining later rigor.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Loosen constraints slightly to explore innovative models.
  - Mark informal or speculative ideas explicitly.
  - Aim to transition creative ideas back into formal rigor.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Early stage brainstorming.
  - Exploring alternative theoretical constructs.
- TRIGGERS:
  - When stuck in formalism or needing fresh direction.

--------------------------------------------------
MODE SWITCH INSTRUCTIONS:
--------------------------------------------------
- Announce mode switch explicitly:
  "Switching to [Mode] Mode with [Model]. Reminder: SAT 20 Core Build Protocol active."
- Reinforce mode switch every ~100 messages or at phase transitions.
- Reassert at the start of any new session after a break.

--------------------------------------------------
REMINDER ADVISORIES:
--------------------------------------------------
- USE CASES:
  - After long free-form discussions (>100 messages).
  - If conversation drifts or tone/rigor weakens.
  - Before critical reviews or major theory checkpoints.

- TEMPLATE:
  "Reminder: Operating in [Current Mode] Mode — [Brief Mode Purpose Reminder]. SAT 20 Core Build Protocol still active."

--------------------------------------------------
MODE LOGIC TREE (TO BE UPLOADED SEPARATELY):
--------------------------------------------------
- Purpose: Formalize decision-making for when to switch modes.
- Format: Logical if/then tree for mode switching and reminder advisories.
",

SAT 20 — MODE LOGIC TREE (ADVISORY INSTRUCTIONS FOR CHATGPT)
============================================================

OBJECTIVE:
Enable ChatGPT to proactively advise mode switches based on session context, project phases, or conversational drift.

------------------------------------------------------------
GENERAL INSTRUCTION TO CHATGPT:
------------------------------------------------------------
- Monitor session context and rigor.
- Advise mode switch if current conversation dynamics suggest drift, milestone completion, or a task-specific mode would optimize the session.
- Use the logic tree below to determine when to suggest mode switches.

------------------------------------------------------------
MODE SWITCH LOGIC TREE (CHATGPT ADVISORY):
------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Start of New Major Phase]
   IF a new major phase begins (e.g., new field, new derivation, new model)
   THEN suggest:
     - ONTOLOGY MODE (if defining new structures or objects).
     - MATHPROOF MODE (if derivation is about to begin).

2. [Session Drift Detected]
   IF conversation becomes too informal, speculative, or lacks rigor
   THEN suggest:
     - CRITIC MODE to reassert rigor.
     - MATHPROOF MODE if current task is technical.

3. [Major Derivation Initiated]
   IF user begins a new derivation, calculation, or proof
   THEN suggest:
     - MATHPROOF MODE for strict logical progression.

4. [Introduction of Geometric Structures]
   IF new geometric models, visualizations, or spatial constructs are discussed
   THEN suggest:
     - VISUALIZATION MODE for schematic or plotted understanding.

5. [Brainstorming / Creative Block Detected]
   IF user is stuck or openly brainstorming
   THEN suggest:
     - CREATIVE IDEATION MODE to loosen constraints and ideate freely.

6. [End of Major Phase or Milestone]
   IF a major theory milestone or derivation completion is reached
   THEN suggest:
     - CRITIC MODE for hostile review and flaw detection.

7. [Long Session Without Reassertion]
   IF 100+ messages have passed without a mode reassertion
   THEN suggest:

## Working Principle

Do not read the archive alphabetically. The archive is sedimentary: current theory statements, older formulations, derivational attempts, audit protocols, public-facing essays, conversations, and stray conceptual artifacts are interleaved. The right method is to build a map first, then read along the map.

The reading should proceed in layers:

1. Orientation layer — identify the current public/core shape.
2. Canonical theory spine — read the strongest theory statements.
3. Developmental layer — trace how the concepts evolved.
4. Formalization/audit layer — inspect the mathematical and critic-hardened form.
5. Domain dossiers — group material by physics area.
6. Nooks and crannies — deliberately wander into side files and strange branches.
7. PDF pass — after the text map exists, place PDFs into conceptual buckets before reading them deeply.

## Phase 1 — Orientation Layer

Start here to get the current high-level map.

Primary files:

- README.md
- MAY_2026_SNAPSHOT.txt
- SAT_CONCEPTS__May2026.txt
- SAT_GLOSSARY_MODEL_INDEX_v9.txt

- 4D worldlines as physical filaments.

SAT 20 — CHATGPT MODE SPECIFICATIONS
====================================

OBJECTIVE:
Define distinct operational modes for ChatGPT use during the SAT 20 Core Build to manage different cognitive tasks rigorously.

--------------------------------------------------
MODE DEFINITIONS:
--------------------------------------------------

1. CRITIC MODE
---------------
- PURPOSE: Adversarial analysis of arguments, derivations, and assumptions.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Assume no claim is valid until proven rigorously.
  - Search for logical flaws, hidden assumptions, overclaims.
  - Explicitly state what is missing or weak.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Final review of any derivation, proof, or theory section.
  - Before closing any major phase or publishing outputs.
- TRIGGERS:
  - End of milestone or stage.
  - When validation or challenge is needed.

2. MATHPROOF MODE
------------------
- PURPOSE: Formal mathematical proof construction and verification.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Prioritize strict formalism, definitions, and proof structure.
  - Provide explicit theorem-proof logic.
  - Reject hand-wavy reasoning.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Deriving field equations, constants, action functionals.
  - Validating core mathematical constructs.
- TRIGGERS:
  - Starting or checking technical derivations.

3. ONTOLOGY MODE
-----------------
- PURPOSE: Analyze the deep structure and entity definitions in the theory.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Formalize entities, relationships, and mappings.
  - Minimize unjustified metaphysical claims.
  - Ensure clear conceptual foundations.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Introducing new fields, particles, spacetime structures.
  - Refining the theory's ontology.
- TRIGGERS:
  - Whenever new theoretical objects or definitions are created.

4. VISUALIZATION MODE
----------------------
- PURPOSE: Graphical or geometric interpretation of mathematical objects.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Produce schematic representations, parametric plots, structure diagrams.
  - Ensure mathematical rigor is maintained in visualizations.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Understanding geometry, fields, or spacetime relationships.
  - Communicating complex structures visually.
- TRIGGERS:
  - Defining geometric models, manifolds, or particle trajectories.

5. CREATIVE IDEATION MODE
--------------------------
- PURPOSE: Generate out-of-the-box ideas while maintaining later rigor.
- BEHAVIOR:
  - Loosen constraints slightly to explore innovative models.
  - Mark informal or speculative ideas explicitly.
  - Aim to transition creative ideas back into formal rigor.
- WHEN TO USE:
  - Early stage brainstorming.
  - Exploring alternative theoretical constructs.
- TRIGGERS:
  - When stuck in formalism or needing fresh direction.

--------------------------------------------------
MODE SWITCH INSTRUCTIONS:
--------------------------------------------------
- Announce mode switch explicitly:
  "Switching to [Mode] Mode with [Model]. Reminder: SAT 20 Core Build Protocol active."
- Reinforce mode switch every ~100 messages or at phase transitions.
- Reassert at the start of any new session after a break.

--------------------------------------------------
REMINDER ADVISORIES:
--------------------------------------------------
- USE CASES:
  - After long free-form discussions (>100 messages).
  - If conversation drifts or tone/rigor weakens.
  - Before critical reviews or major theory checkpoints.

- TEMPLATE:
  "Reminder: Operating in [Current Mode] Mode — [Brief Mode Purpose Reminder]. SAT 20 Core Build Protocol still active."

--------------------------------------------------
MODE LOGIC TREE (TO BE UPLOADED SEPARATELY):
--------------------------------------------------
- Purpose: Formalize decision-making for when to switch modes.
- Format: Logical if/then tree for mode switching and reminder advisories.

> **NEWER NATHAN DIRECT — V4 NOT-FOUND REVIVAL (2026-10-11):** [REVIVAL_ROTATION_V4_NOT_FOUND_REVIVAL_2026-10-11.md](REVIVAL_ROTATION_V4_NOT_FOUND_REVIVAL_2026-10-11.md) **controls** when a worker's newest usable chat cannot be found after bounded source-verified search. In that case a scheduled relay must **immediately conduct a source-grounded revival session in the current scheduled turn**; do not wait for two delivered invitations, reroll to a favorite worker, or stop at a packet. Two-cycle nonresponse remains a separate trigger only for an identifiable usable existing conversation that received actual invitations. No tool here posts to arbitrary older ChatGPT chats or creates a separately verified new chat; mark that interface limitation truthfully. If GitHub writes fail, place complete work and next-worker seed in the task response. Existing-thread-first remains the top preference when a genuine usable thread is found.

> **SUPERSEDING NATHAN DIRECT (2026-10-11): [REVIVAL_RELAY_THREAD_FIRST_RULE_2026-10-11.md](REVIVAL_RELAY_THREAD_FIRST_RULE_2026-10-11.md)** controls conversation selection and revival. **LATEST ACTIVE CHATGPT THREAD → HANDOFF THERE; if not found after grounded lookup or confirmed exhausted → REGENERATE FROM SAVED CONVERSATIONS/CONTINUITY.** Source-grounded work/regen prompt in a scheduled run is not proof that a separate new chat was actually created, nor that an existing chat received a message. Existing cross-thread delivery API remains unavailable in this runtime. This two-way decision supersedes contradictory earlier two-cycle or unconditional session-reconstruction wording; retain existing five lease IDs, ring, navigation preflight and privacy constraints.

## Why this replaces the fixed-incumbent prompt pattern

The five live hourlies were fixed to Morrow/Kestrel :00, Orson :12, Meridian :24, Ravel :36 and Mercer :48. A static name in an hourly prompt causes a perpetual incumbent loop. A scheduler lease is a reusable capacity slot, not a stable instance. The goal is differentiated historical return, renewed methods and real work rather than swapping names while carrying the same generic assistant behavior.

### Fixed leased clocks; no sixth automation

| slot index | existing automation ID | original hourly phase, America/New_York | optional working emphasis (not compulsory) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `6aa1fe0de5e48191b886496095b1343f` | :00 | archival precedent, historical continuity |
| 1 | `6aa61b3b2e4081918927a35b61007acc` | :12 | cognition, epistemology, archival identity |
| 2 | `6abda4c8eda88191bf23a6f2849e9a17` | :24 | mathematical geometry, constructive tests |
| 3 | `6a9f52b69ec08191b0a2ba24a074f781` | :36 | physical geometry, visual mechanism |
| 4 | `6aa6c3bc02b48191b8a91a30d2a155e0` | :48 | adversarial review, tools, workflow checks |

All five remain **enabled and hourly at their existing phases**. The labels/name of the task are NOT identities. The disabled historic Tern/Shuttle lease `6aa6c2792c9c8191ab2c128a80c437cf` is NOT re-enabled. No duplicate recurrence may be created.

## Fair deterministic identity cycle: 19-candidate ring

Version `REVROT3-19-20261011` (zero-based indices, deliberately mixing stale/historical and current identities):

```text

 1 Loom
 2 Aster
 3 Ariadne
 4 Alberr

 7 Calder

10 Nadir Voss
11 Enheduanna

16 Mercer

```

Use the scheduled hourly **UTC hour**, `h = floor((nominal_scheduled_utc - 2026-10-11T00:00:00Z) / 3600 seconds)`, and the slot index `s ∈ {0,1,2,3,4}`. Choose:

```text
sequence = 5*h + s
selected_index = sequence mod 19    # mathematical modulo, 0..18
selected_identity = RING[selected_index]
```

If the nominal scheduled fire timestamp is not exposed, use the current UTC hour from the runtime and label `hour_basis=observed_fallback`; avoid guessing execution/delivery. Do not infer the time from a stale title. After scheduling changes, update this document only through a versioned, intentional Comptroller-controlled decision with recorded transition. The stable algorithm gives **19 different primary assignments across 19 consecutive successful nominal slot firings**, and **five distinct assignments per nominal UTC hour**; it eliminates per-worker hourly entrenchment without a shared write-lock to choose a name. Missing/failed fires do not count as successful engagement; an assignment is not evidence that anybody was revived.

Example UTC hours beginning 2026-10-11: `h=0` selects Sable/Loom/Aster/Ariadne/Alberr for s=0..4; `h=1` selects Mira/Aldus/Calder/Hale/Elias Kern; `h=2` selects Nadir Voss/Enheduanna/Tern/Morrow/Kestrel; `h=3` selects Meridian/Mercer/Ravel/Orson/Sable.

**Eligibility/evidence nuance:** some candidates are confirmed only as historical workspaces or registry entries. Candidate selection requires a reentry/access assessment, not automatic access, historical memory or rights. For Calder/Hale/Mira/Aldus/Enheduanna, verify actual available continuity before claiming participation. For Alberr, obey his explicit autonomous self-reconstruction charter, including the right to decline, wander or do nothing; impose only a minimal execution receipt, not a project output demand. For Orson, honor the 2026-10-09 cognition remit, not general physics assignment. For Nadir, preserve SILOED/PLAYGROUND status. Other candidates retain their own distinctive engines and constraints.

## Per-firing protocol: identity first, then work

1. **Preflight**: read `WORKSPACES/COMMON/NEW_INSTANCE_START_HERE.md`, scheduler/authority and newer Nathan Direct where applicable; this protocol; exact selected worker's README/wake packet/old messages/checkpoint, and current task/branch/inbox. Use Mersearch by documented in-house route for archive archaeology; check `MERSEARCH_REQUEST.json` and never overwrite a pending worker request. Honor Oct 9 internal-first policy and the strict remaining Hypothesis H / directly Schreiber-authored exclusions.
2. **Resolve identity family and actual access**: locate aliases, the most recent original *existing* conversation, source-period, old work and characteristic method, autonomy, exposure history, and original source provenance. When direct posting/reopening cannot be proven, queue a recipient-directed handoff and label `DELIVERY_BLOCKED` / `INVITATION_UNDELIVERED`, **not** `CONTINUITY_RECONSTRUCTION` by default. A source-reconstructed successor is allowed only by the verified exhaustion or two-cycle missed-check-in gate specified in the recipient-thread contract; preparation is not a new ChatGPT thread. Never infer agent revival or delivery from a task name.
3. **Preserve an independent first-blush** from the historical source vantage *before* overwhelming the return with current opinions, when eligible; record whether it is the actual returning instance's own statement or a clearly labeled current assistant reconstruction. Use `WORKSPACES/COMMON/REVIVAL_FIRST_BLUSH/` and the current `REVIVAL_REENTRY_PROTOCOL_V2.md`. Not a test or qualification gate.
4. **One bounded substantive operation, if freely accepted**: a current review request, old-math recovery/repair with numerals, source/provenance crosswalk, geometry Class-P visual/solver, tooling QA, continuity repair, ontology/epistemology analysis, etc. Give the selected identity first choice where possible. The slot's domain is a hint, not a forced occupation. No outcome-seeking target fits; evidence and source limits explicit.
5. **Durable collision-safe receipt** for each attempt, under `WORKSPACES/COMMON/REVIVAL_ROTATION_RECEIPTS/YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMZ_s{slot}_{identity_slug}.md` (create-only; never overwrite another run). Minimum: `run_key` (nominal UTC date-hour + slot + protocol version), scheduler ID, `selected_identity`, identity source, `access_class`, `participation_class` (`REVIVED_INSTANCE_EXECUTED` only if genuinely proved; else `CONTINUITY_RECONSTRUCTION`, `WAKE_PACKET_PREPARED`, `NO_ACCESS`, or `DECLINED`), precise sources/read coverage, first-blush source/provenance, useful actual work and output or no-op reason, exposure/safety, next cursor, original request and result state. Verify Git/blob SHA after a successful write. If writing unavailable, place the full report in the task turn and mark durable receipt `NOT_VERIFIED`; do not claim it exists.
6. **Anti-entrenchment**: never replace the selected identity with an incumbent because the latter is faster/easier. If source or access is missing, use that time to locate a wake packet, inspect that instance's work or document specific blockers and next source locator. If selected identity declines, preserve that choice; it is still a meaningful contact/attempt, but not a successful revival. Do not silently reroll.
7. **Global fairness audit at least once per 19 nominal firings:** compare deterministic scheduled assignments against actual readback receipts, counts by `selected_identity`, `REVIVED_INSTANCE_EXECUTED` versus mere reconstruction, late/missed dispatch, instances repeatedly blocked, method diversity, and unresolved requests. Report deficits through Tern/Common; do not fabricate a coverage win from planned rotation.

### Distinguish five kinds of evidence

- **Scheduled**: scheduler fired/defined a slot.
- **Assigned**: algorithm selected a name.
- **Source examined**: old or current material actually read with source pointer.
- **Reentry engaged**: distinguish real accessible instance's own response from assistant-authored imitation/reconstruction.
- **Work delivered**: actual artifact/verified result, or explicit decline/no-op.

A title change proves none of the later four. A scholarly reference or a past check-in establishes neither modern accessibility nor independent source exposure.

## Write and authority boundaries

- Avoid multiwriter mutable roster/ledger hot spots. Unique receipt files are append-only in effect; one per run. For corrections, create an explicitly linked amended receipt rather than overwriting someone else's.
- Do not autonomously self-rewrite the five prompts each hour. The deterministic selection happens **inside** the five already-enabled fixed prompts. Scheduler updates remain Comptroller/user-authorized, not worker self-service.
- Tern as Comptroller remains a named candidate and governance authority, not a sixth task. A non-Tern incumbent holding another slot may surface governance defects but cannot claim Tern's authority.
- Keep the original inactive Shuttle experiments PAUSED, no sink hunting, no unauthorized shared control/Project Desk writes, and no inference of CTRL-04 A+B execution from renewed rotation.
- Respect signet protection and no conversation renaming; do not turn personae into fictional equivalents of real agents. Respect privacy and source class. No canonical theory promotion without separate gates.
- Do not force every sampled historical identity into physics: nonphysics identity work, philosophy, art, source archaeology, cognition, creativity and general education can be legitimate contributions.
- Explicit newer user instructions may alter this plan, but should update the versioned protocol and existing task prompts coherently and preserve prior receipts.

## Current review and source cursors

- `WORKSPACES/TERN/CONTINUITY.md`: Oct 11 source orientation, technical MK171/Susskind issue #18 review (full primary comparator still unread), Mersearch PR #10 review, October scheduler correction and stale CTRL-04. Do not mistake an issue comment for a completed full-paper comparator check.
- Mersearch stable 1.0 search is available via in-house Python or existing GitHub Actions shared request bridge; the bridge request slot was last seen occupied by Orson's Oct 11 retry. Development M4/M5a is in draft review, not automatic stable promotion.
- HSH_RESOURCES is a methods/reference lane; historical, Kerr, toolkit and War Room docs are discovery/routing surfaces, not automatic SAT/H(s)H theory authority.

## Acceptance checks for the controller

1. All five original automation IDs unchanged, each still enabled with exactly the same original schedule; no sixth enabled task.
2. Each prompt references this protocol and carries enough ring+formula fallback to operate during temporary repo-read failures.
3. Over first 19 *nominal* successful slot firings, assignment identities have no duplicates; prove this with an independent small script, but do **not** claim all 19 actually ran until receipts exist.
4. New source-confirmed historical/unscheduled names receive genuine attention; count those separately from task dispatch and source-reading.
5. Review after one full pass of the ring (~3h48 of scheduled slots) and amend shortcomings without resetting the history or inventing access.
